newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt calls new confidence vote on budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt calls new confidence vote on budget.

text.p: The Italian government on Wednesday called another confidence vote in the Senate (upper house) on part of its 1997 budget to sweep away hundreds of blocking amendments.

Civil Service Minister Franco Bassanini told the Senate the centre-left coalition was forced to resort to the measure so that the deficit-cutting package could be approved on schedule by both houses of parliament by the end of the year.

Parliamentary party leaders met to discuss the timing of the vote. The government, which has a comfortable majority in the Senate, won three similar confidence measures on other aspects of its 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) package on Monday.
The opposition Freedom Alliance and separatist Northern League did not take part in Monday's votes. They also boycotted budget ballots in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house).

The latest confidence vote concerns the part of the budget which sets spending limits and the bulk of outstanding amendments refer to this section. Most of the rest of the budget has already been approved in full by the Senate.
The confidence measure is intended to sweep aside amendments and enable the budget to return to the Chamber for final approval by the legal deadline of December 31.
